industries.name: Coffee Shop
audiences: remote workers who treat the café as an office
contexts: {client} is an independent roastery with three sites in the city. Word of mouth has carried them this far, but their visual identity was made in a hurry when they opened and no longer matches the quality in the cup.
{client} has just secured a lease on a fourth location and wants everything they put in front of customers to look like it came from the same company.
{client} is preparing to introduce a {product} and needs it to feel like a genuine event rather than another item on the board.
objectives: introduce the {product} to existing regulars
attract a younger weekday audience without alienating loyal customers
raise average spend per visit
build recognition ahead of a fourth location opening
competitors: a well-funded speciality rival two streets away

industries.name: Fitness Studio
contexts: {client} is a member-owned studio that has grown from a garage set-up to a two-floor space. Their marketing still looks like the garage.
{client} wants to shift perception away from intimidating hardcore training and towards steady, welcoming progress.
{client} is launching a {product} in January, the busiest and most competitive month of their year.
objectives: fill the {product} before the January rush
reduce the number of members who cancel in month two
position the studio as welcoming rather than intimidating
grow off-peak daytime attendance

industries.name: Technology Startup
audiences: operations leads at companies of 50–500 people
IT decision makers in mid-market firms
contexts: {client} closed a seed round four months ago and is moving from a founder-led sales motion to a self-serve product. Everything customer-facing was built by engineers in a hurry.
{client} is preparing to present at a large industry conference and needs a coherent look across stand, site and slides.
{client} is launching their {product} and has one shot at a first impression with a sceptical technical audience.
objectives: convert trial sign-ups into paying accounts
explain a complicated product in one screen
look established enough to be trusted with company data
support the launch of the {product}
competitors: two heavily funded rivals with bigger design teams
an entrenched legacy tool everyone complains about

industries.name: Restaurant
audiences: locals looking for a weeknight dinner
contexts: {client} is a neighbourhood restaurant with a new head chef and a menu that has changed considerably. The printed material has not kept up.
{client} is opening a second site across town and needs the identity to travel without losing its character.
{client} is introducing a {product} and wants covers to increase on quiet nights.
objectives: fill tables on quiet weeknights
communicate a menu change without confusing regulars
raise the perceived price point honestly
support the {product}
competitors: a popular chain restaurant on the same street
the venue that photographs better on social media

industries.name: Fashion Brand
audiences: sustainability-minded buyers willing to pay more
long-standing customers who buy every season
contexts: {client} sells mainly online and is preparing their {product}. Their previous launch looked inconsistent across email, social and site.
{client} has grown quickly through one viral product and now needs an identity that can carry a full range.
{client} is entering physical retail for the first time and needs packaging and in-store material that matches the online experience.
objectives: sell through the {product} within six weeks
raise the perceived quality of the brand
make sustainability claims credible rather than decorative
build a look that works across every channel
competitors: fast-fashion retailers with far bigger budgets

industries.name: Sustainable Goods
contexts: {client} makes a {product} that genuinely performs well, but on shelf it is beaten by rivals with louder packaging and vaguer claims.
{client} is a certified B Corporation whose visual identity does not yet communicate the rigour behind the certification.
{client} is moving from a market stall to national retail listings and needs everything to be production ready.
objectives: stand out on a crowded shelf without shouting
explain the refill system in one glance
make the environmental claim specific and verifiable
support entry into national retail
competitors: mainstream brands with recent green rebrands
direct-to-consumer rivals with strong social presence

industries.name: Healthcare Clinic
audiences: patients aged 45 and over who prefer clear print material
young families registering with a new practice
people nervous about visiting a clinic
contexts: {client} has merged with a neighbouring practice. Patients are receiving conflicting information and the two sets of signage do not match.
{client} is introducing an {product} and many patients are unsure how to use it.
{client} needs material that is calm and legible for readers with low vision, without feeling clinical or cold.
objectives: reduce missed appointments
make the {product} easy for every age group to use
reassure anxious patients
meet accessibility expectations in every printed item
competitors: private clinics with larger marketing budgets

industries.name: Education Provider
contexts: {client} runs an excellent {product} that almost nobody outside their existing student body has heard of.
{client} is competing for applications against institutions with far bigger reach and needs to look serious and current.
{client} has an open day in six weeks and every piece of material must work in print, on screen and on campus signage.
objectives: increase applications for the {product}
reach an audience that has never considered this kind of course
explain outcomes and cost honestly
drive attendance at the open day

industries.name: Music & Events
audiences: local music fans who follow venues rather than bands
contexts: {client} is announcing their {product} and needs one visual idea that survives being cropped, screen-printed and posted at thumbnail size.
{client} books a mixture of genres and needs an identity flexible enough to host all of them without becoming bland.
{client} sells most tickets through social media, where their material currently gets lost.
objectives: sell out the {product}
make the announcement instantly recognisable in a busy feed
build a look that carries across posters, tickets and merchandise
attract an audience beyond the existing regulars
competitors: streaming platforms competing for the same attention
free events in the same week

industries.name: Financial Services
contexts: {client} is launching a {product} aimed at people who find financial products intimidating and jargon-heavy.
{client} must present regulated information clearly while still looking like a company somebody would choose.
{client} is a long-established firm whose material looks dated next to app-based competitors.
objectives: make a regulated product feel understandable
attract a younger customer without losing existing trust
present required legal information without burying the message
support the launch of the {product}

industries.name: Travel & Hospitality
contexts: {client} has strong reviews and weak bookings between October and March. The {product} is designed to fix that.
{client} is opening a new property and needs everything from signage to booking confirmation to feel like one place.
{client} competes with listings platforms where every property looks the same.
objectives: increase off-season bookings
make direct booking more attractive than third-party platforms
communicate the character of the place in a single image
support the {product}
competitors: larger hotel groups with loyalty schemes

industries.name: Beauty & Skincare
audiences: shoppers aged 25–40 who read ingredient lists
first-time buyers of a skincare routine
contexts: {client} is launching a {product} into a category where every competitor uses the same minimal beige packaging.
{client} makes evidence-led products but their packaging currently promises magic rather than method.
{client} is preparing for a retail listing where the product will be seen for two seconds at arm's length.
objectives: be distinguishable at arm's length on shelf
communicate the active ingredient clearly
avoid unsupported claims while still feeling premium
launch the {product}

industries.name: Non-Profit
contexts: {client} runs a {product} every year and the response has fallen for three years running. The material has not changed in that time.
{client} must show where money goes without resorting to imagery that strips people of dignity.
{client} has a tiny budget, no photography and one volunteer designer.
objectives: increase donations to the {product}
show impact with numbers rather than sentiment
recruit volunteers from outside the usual circle
produce material that can be printed cheaply in black and one colour

industries.name: Real Estate
contexts: {client} is launching a {product} of 48 apartments and needs material that sells the neighbourhood, not just the floor plans.
{client} looks identical to every other agent in town: same photography, same typeface, same green.
{client} needs a brochure that works both as an expensive printed piece and as a downloadable file.
objectives: reserve units before construction completes
differentiate from identical local competitors
make complicated floor-plan information readable
support the {product}

industries.name: Gaming & Esports
contexts: {client} is announcing a {product} and competing for attention in feeds full of high-budget publisher campaigns.
{client} has an energetic community but a visual identity assembled from stock assets and default typefaces.
{client} needs assets that read clearly as a small thumbnail and as a large stage screen.
objectives: build wishlist sign-ups before launch
look credible next to much larger publishers
create a mark the community will want on merchandise
support the {product}
competitors: the sheer volume of new releases each week

industries.name: Creative Agency
contexts: {client} does strong work for clients and has neglected their own identity for four years.
{client} is repositioning from generalist design services towards a specialism and everything must communicate the shift.
{client} is preparing a {product} and needs a case for their own taste to be self-evident.
objectives: attract better-fitting clients rather than more clients
demonstrate the studio's point of view in the work itself
support recruitment
launch the {product}

industries.name: Food Product
contexts: {client} is launching a {product} into a supermarket category where shoppers decide in under three seconds.
{client} sells well at markets where the founder can explain the product, and poorly on shelves where nobody can.
{client} needs one packaging system that can carry four flavours without four separate designs.
objectives: be identifiable at three metres and readable at thirty centimetres
make the range structure obvious across flavours
meet legal labelling requirements without losing the design
launch the {product}
competitors: other new entrants with similar positioning

industries.name: Professional Services
contexts: {client} is a serious firm whose material looks either dated or indistinguishable from every competitor.
{client} is launching a {product} and needs to look modern without losing the authority clients expect.
{client} needs templates that non-designers in the firm can use without ruining them.
objectives: look contemporary while remaining credible
make dense information genuinely readable
produce templates that survive internal use
support the {product}

industries.name: Pet Care
contexts: {client} is launching a {product} in a category dominated by either cartoon cuteness or clinical veterinary styling.
{client} wants to be warm without being childish, and trustworthy without being cold.
{client} needs packaging that photographs well when customers share their unboxing.
objectives: build a monthly subscriber base
look trustworthy to owners spending on their pets
encourage customers to share the product
launch the {product}

industries.name: Automotive
audiences: drivers considering their first electric vehicle
contexts: {client} is launching a {product} and must explain an unfamiliar service to people who have never used one.
{client} needs signage, app screens and print material that all feel like the same company.
{client} competes in a category where trust is the entire purchase decision.
objectives: explain an unfamiliar service simply
build trust with sceptical buyers
make wayfinding and signage unmistakable
launch the {product}

industries.name: Home & Interiors
contexts: {client} makes furniture to order and needs material that explains a longer wait as a benefit rather than a problem.
{client} is launching a {product} and needs the catalogue, site and showroom to agree with each other.
{client} sells a considered product in a market trained to expect next-day delivery.
objectives: justify a premium price honestly
make a complex configurable product easy to understand
drive showroom visits
launch the {product}
competitors: independent makers with strong social followings

industries.name: Sports Club
contexts: {client} is a community club whose crest and colours carry a century of meaning that cannot be discarded.
{client} is launching a {product} and needs to reach families who have never attended a match.
{client} needs matchday material that works on a stadium screen, a printed programme and a phone.
objectives: grow attendance among families
respect club heritage while modernising
attract sponsors with a professional look
support the {product}

industries.name: Media & Publishing
audiences: readers who buy single issues at newsstands
younger readers discovering the title online
contexts: {client} is redesigning after fifteen years and must keep long-standing readers while attracting new ones.
{client} is launching a {product} and needs a system rather than a single beautiful layout.
{client} competes on the newsstand where the cover is the entire sales pitch.
objectives: increase newsstand pick-up
convert readers into subscribers
create a layout system others can follow issue after issue
launch the {product}
competitors: social platforms competing for reading time

industries.name: Logistics
contexts: {client} operates a reliable service with material that looks like it was made in a word processor.
{client} is launching a {product} and needs to explain it to buyers who care about cost and reliability, not aesthetics.
{client} needs an identity that survives being applied to vehicles, high-visibility clothing and one-colour printing.
objectives: look as professional as the service actually is
make a technical offer easy to compare
produce an identity that works in one colour on a vehicle
launch the {product}
